reason: Ask B gives identity editing a clear scope and completion action, then restores the spacious composer. Why A makes the complete reasoning readable with the fewest operations. Neither meets the authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold across screens and components. C's Cancel behavior and prototype focus replacement are concrete browser issues, independent of deferred native testing.
limitations: Scores combine normal and 200% evidence for each of eight screen/variant pairs. Component tuples use [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]; null means genuinely inapplicable or outside the implemented prototype behavior.
Inspected only supplied images, checks.json and expansion-18.html. No browser drive, implementation, delegation, previous grades or research. Source findings are not runtime verification.

checks.json records content preservation and no horizontal overflow for all twelve alternative size combinations. It does not document individual actions, focus results, target measurements, errors or assistive-technology outcomes.

Baseline runtime evidence was supplied by the brief. Alternatives do not inherit its engine, export, motion, keyboard or performance results. Inert prototype exit, voice and forecast-return controls are excluded from behavioral certification.

No demonstrated hard-gate failure is assigned within the implemented comparison scope. Offscreen content alone is not treated as inaccessible. Cancel retaining edits is a recovery defect; no data loss is demonstrated.

Physical iPhone, VoiceOver and other native checks remain unverified. Browser scores are provisional; no full/native 9/10 certification is granted. Contrast, complete state coverage and transition continuity are not established by these images and aggregate checks.
